# generator-shortcuts

## Strongest simple rival I tested

**Match pieces using only their top two rows, ignoring the bottom row when choosing
the candidate.** Greedily choose the first unused colored candidate whose top-two
row lengths complement the current cyan piece. Then fill the actual cyan piece's
remaining cells with that selected color. The rival still uses the whole cyan
shape when painting; the omitted information is the bottom-row shape in the
matching decision, not the bottom row of the output.

This is registered as `ignore_row_2`. It fits all three canonical demonstrations
and even the fourth supplied public canonical pair (4/4). It also achieves
360/360 correct outputs in the before cohort, source `f9dd076407f0f99a42138fb70d3024115908f44d6f330270ad93fbfffb9f2440`, seeds `1000..1119`,
indices `0..119` independently in each band. Thus this is not an invented
wrong rule that was already trivially contradicted by the supplied examples.
I do not claim it is the strongest rival among every possible program.

The mechanism is exact: when all cyan cuts sum to six, knowing two row lengths
uniquely determines the third. No amount of recoloring or positional diversity
removes this shortcut while the fixed-area constraint remains.

## Exact disagreement emitted by the final generator

Final source SHA-256: `cca4fcc91281d89167c1720318f997267741052520e441a5266b17ac11b8b95c`. Call
`generate(1010, 10, difficulty="easy")`, with no overrides. The resulting 9×11
input is below; each digit is one ARC cell, with background 7 and anchor color 8.

```text
77777777777
88777777222
87777772222
88777777772
77777777777
88777777333
87777773333
88887777333
77777777777
```

The first cyan cut is `(2,1,2)` and the second is `(2,1,4)`. The candidates, in
input order, are color 2 for the second cut and color 3 for the first. Both cuts
agree in the top two rows. The rival therefore assigns color 2 to the first
anchor and color 3 to the second, whereas the full shape relation does the reverse.

Actual selected Racket output:

```text
77777777777
88333777777
83333777777
88333777777
77777777777
88222777777
82222777777
88882777777
77777777777
```

Rival output:

```text
77777777777
88222777777
82222777777
88222777777
77777777777
88333777777
83333777777
88883777777
77777777777
```

## How it was checked

`checks/final-census-v3/witness_ignore_row_2.json` stores the exact input, both
outputs, seed/index/band, empty override map, source/rule hashes, validator result,
command and actual runtime directory. The input passed `self_check`. The output
was obtained from the real selected Racket oracle, not accepted solely because
it matched my Python mirror. Independent reconstruction agrees with Racket.

Reproducer from the extracted packet root, using a new empty runtime path:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 generators/54a83e6bbc20/workspace/run_review.py \
  --action census --phase final --out ../checks/replay-census \
  --runtime /tmp/arcpuzzles-54a83-replay --per-band 200 --oracle-samples 40 --width-sweep
```

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases without forced overrides. The final
cohort has `ignore_row_2` correct on 440/600 draw instances, so 160/600 disagree.
Top- and middle-row omission rivals are separately registered and witnessed.
The three-demo schedule excludes surviving rivals that would change the next
query, rather than requiring every single draw to distinguish all rivals.
These are distribution/lesson results, not evidence of improved trained-model
accuracy.
